# Hand washing with soap (`hand_hygiene`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/medicine.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Medicine & hygiene (`medicine`)
- Deps: needs soap; helped by contagion_theory, chlorine_bleach, controlled_trial
- Core idea: Hands carry disease from excrement, corpses, pus and the sick to mouths, food, wounds and women in labour. Wet the hands, rub soap over every surface for about 20 seconds (backs, between the fingers, thumbs, under short-cut nails), rinse under poured or running water, not in a shared basin, and dry on a clean cloth or in the air. Always after defecating or cleaning a child, before preparing food and eating, before and after touching a wound, a patient or a birth, and after touching the dead. Surgery calls for surgical hand antisepsis before sterile gloves. Chlorinated lime was a historical intervention: in Semmelweis's Vienna clinic, deaths of mothers fell from about one in ten to about one in a hundred once students washed in chlorinated lime after autopsies.
- Pitfalls:
  - A quick rinse in water, or in a basin everyone shares, which spreads the dirt around
  - Thinking only visible dirt or bad smell matters; Semmelweis's students had hands that looked clean
  - Washing only after the work instead of before touching the patient or the food
  - Drying on a dirty common towel or apron
  - Assuming gloves replace hand hygiene; hands can be contaminated while removing them
- History: india: early centuries AD – Sushruta Samhita asks the surgeon to be clean with short nails and hair (dating disputed); islamic: 7th c. onward – ritual washing before prayer and meals makes frequent washing habitual, without soap or a disease theory; europe: 1795 – Gordon (Aberdeen) shows childbed fever is carried by attendants; 1847 Semmelweis introduces chlorinated-lime hand washing in Vienna: first clinic mortality about 11 % in 1846, about 1.3 % in 1848; americas: 1843 – Oliver Wendell Holmes argues in Boston that attendants can carry childbed fever; global: 2005 – trial in Karachi squatter settlements: soap and hand-washing promotion halves childhood diarrhoea and pneumonia
- Read:
  - Ignaz Semmelweis, Die Aetiologie, der Begriff und die Prophylaxis des Kindbettfiebers (1861)
  - Sherwin B. Nuland, The Doctors' Plague (2003)
  - Stephen P. Luby et al., Effect of handwashing on child health: a randomised controlled trial, The Lancet (2005)
